title: Two and a half per cent
word: Two and a half per cent

segments.voice: Yesterday, nisab, the threshold, and your line: the line of wealth. Did you look up where the line sits today? Now, for wealth above it, how much? Day one thousand ninety-six.

Forty dates in a bowl, counted out by hand onto a plate. Thirty-nine of them go back to be eaten, shared, saved. One of them, just one, is set apart on the edge of the plate. That's it. That's the whole share. When people first hear zakat described as a pillar of the faith, a duty that sits beside the prayer, some expect it to be heavy. A tenth, a quarter, half. Then comes the number, and it's small. Small enough to keep doing, every year, for a whole life. Today, one coin out of forty: two and a half percent.
screen: `FORTY DATES IN A BOWL.` → `ONE SET APART.` → `SMALLER THAN SOME EXPECT.`

segments.voice: First, the words the hadith use. In Sahih al-Bukhari there's a letter that Abu Bakr wrote setting out the rules of zakat, and for silver it gives the share as rub' al-'ushr. A quarter of a tenth. Take a tenth, then take a quarter of that, and you have one fortieth. Two and a half percent. Second, the same share, counted in coins. A report in the Sunan of Abu Dawud has the Prophet ﷺ say to bring a quarter of a tenth, one dirham from every forty. And the threshold you met yesterday says it the same way: on two hundred dirhams, five. Two hundred divided by forty is five. The numbers in these reports agree with each other. Third, what it's charged on. Not on income as it flows in, and not on everything you own. On saved wealth above the line, held a year: cash, savings, gold and silver, goods for trade. Teachers of the law don't count your home, the clothes you wear, or the car you drive to work in the same way, and a later day looks at the categories one by one. Fourth, why such a small share might be the point. A share this size is something a person can give every year without being ruined by it, and the people who receive it can count on it coming, year after year. Small, and steady, and owed. A quarter of a tenth doesn't ask you to give everything. It asks for something, reliably, year after year. Which is harder than it sounds. Anyone can be generous once. Zakat asks for one in forty, every single year.
screen: `A QUARTER OF A TENTH.` · `ONE DIRHAM FROM EVERY FORTY.` · `ON SAVED WEALTH ABOVE THE LINE.` · `SMALL, STEADY, OWED.` · then, large: `ONE IN FORTY.`

segments.voice: The practice: work out one fortieth of your savings. You can do it in your head, the old way. Take whatever number you have in mind, savings, or just a round figure if you'd rather not think about your own. Divide it by ten. Then divide that by four. That's a quarter of a tenth. Hold that number. Breathe in, and notice how big or small it feels next to the whole. Breathe out, and picture the thirty-nine parts that stay. The bell holds the time.
Two and a half percent. Rub' al-'ushr, a quarter of a tenth: one fortieth of saved wealth above the threshold. Today's word.
screen: `TWO AND A HALF PER CENT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: one in forty. Today, when you see a price or a total, find one fortieth of it in your head: divide by ten, then by four. Tomorrow: the year, and how long wealth has to sit. Day one thousand ninety-six.

howItsDone: Muslims who owe zakat on money and savings give one fortieth, two and a half percent, of what they hold above the nisab, once a year, some using a mosque's or charity's zakat calculator.

trapdoor: what you thought: zakat must be a heavy share, a tenth or more.
what it means: on saved wealth above the line, one in forty, two and a half percent, once a year.
what a scholar hears: rub' al-'ushr, a quarter of a tenth, the phrase in Abu Bakr's letter of zakat in Bukhari.

notes: Bukhari 1454 (Abu Bakr's letter; 'in silver, a quarter of a tenth'): confirm number and that rub' al-'ushr appears there.
Abu Dawud 1572 (bring a quarter of a tenth, one dirham from every forty): confirm number and grading.

Teach says the home, clothes and a work car are 'not counted in the same way'; that's the general position drawn from Bukhari 1463 (no sadaqah on a Muslim's horse or slave), cited on day 1098. Confirm.
Index title spells 'per cent'; the voice says 'percent' (American spelling); the title and word are kept exactly.
